note: Golden vectors of the loop law (CONTRACT §5a). Every implementation of the law runs every case: plan `spec` against `ctx`, then step tick by tick. A tick's `inputs` are the readings by signal name (null = no value), `dt` is the time since the previous tick in ms, `set` ({params, ramp_ms?}) changes params ahead of the tick. `expect.outputs` has one value per output, equal within 1e-9; `guard` and `end` are present exactly on the tick that ends the loop.

cases.name: term of value with a setpoint
term of derivative: the setpoint is a rate, the first tick has none, dt is the measured one
term of integral with a clamp, and a gain that is a param
term of integral without a clamp keeps growing while the output is cut
feed terms, params, and params set with and without a ramp
a setpoint that is a param follows its ramp
zero start subtracts the first reading
zero mean: outputs are 0 while it measures, the law starts on the tick after, zero start took the first reading
zero mean that saw motion ends the loop with not_still
detrend subtracts a running mean that starts at the first reading
smooth is a first-order low-pass that starts at the first reading; the derivative is of the smoothed value
an output is cut to its limit and to the range of the argument it drives
guard gt ends the loop on the tick it holds, with outputs at 0
guard lt with for_ms holds in a row, then ends the loop
guard abs_gt on the integral of a signal
guard on a derivative; the first guard of the list that holds gives the name
a tick without a value holds the signal; the derivative spans the gap; the third in a row ends the loop with input_lost
